title: Performance Obligations - Identification and Analysis Under ASC 606
learning_objectives: Master the definition and identification of performance obligations
Distinguish between separate POs and combined POs
Understand series provision for repetitive services
Apply performance obligation concepts to CPA exam scenarios

common_question_types: Identifying number of performance obligations in a contract

fundamental_concepts.definition: A performance obligation is a promise in a contract with a customer to transfer to the customer either: (a) a good or service (or a bundle of goods or services) that is distinct, or (b) a series of distinct goods or services that are substantially the same and that have the same pattern of transfer to the customer.
fundamental_concepts.importance: Performance obligation identification is Step 2 of the five-step model and is critical because:
why_it_matters: Determines how transaction price is allocated (Step 4)
Directly tested on CPA exam through scenarios
fundamental_concepts.key_principle: The unit of account for revenue recognition is the performance obligation, not the contract or the individual goods/services listed in the contract.

explicit_promises.description: Goods or services explicitly stated in the contract
examples: Product delivery specified in purchase order
Services listed in statement of work
Deliverables enumerated in project schedule

implicit_promises.description: Goods or services not explicitly stated but implied by entity's customary business practices, published policies, or specific statements
examples: Free shipping if entity's website states 'all orders ship free'
Free technical support if entity always provides it even if not contractually required
Customary setup activities that customers expect
Installation services routinely provided without separate charge
implicit_promises.key_point: Past practices create implicit promises even if not written in current contract

activities_that_are_not_promises.description: Not all activities in fulfilling a contract transfer goods or services to the customer

examples: Setting up internal systems to track contract
Obtaining contract approvals internally
Allocating resources to contract
excluded_activities.rationale: These are internal activities that don't transfer goods/services to customer

examples: Mobilizing workforce and equipment to job site (if setup doesn't transfer goods/services)
Initial project planning that benefits entity, not customer
excluded_activities.rationale: If activities don't result in transfer of good/service, not a performance obligation
excluded_activities.exception: If setup activities result in asset customer controls, they may be part of performance obligation

immaterial_promises.principle: An entity need not assess whether promises are performance obligations if they are immaterial in the context of the contract with the customer
immaterial_promises.key_point: Materiality assessed at contract level, not entity level
examples: Free promotional item of nominal value included with purchase
Incidental services that cost entity very little
Complimentary items customers don't value
immaterial_promises.cpa_exam_tip: If exam question doesn't emphasize a particular item or describes it as 'incidental,' treat as immaterial

distinct_criteria.overview: A good or service is DISTINCT if BOTH of the following criteria are met. Meeting only one criterion is insufficient - both are required.

criterion_1_capable_of_being_distinct.title: Criterion 1: Capable of Being Distinct
criterion_1_capable_of_being_distinct.definition: The customer can benefit from the good or service either on its own or together with other resources that are readily available to the customer.
criterion_1_capable_of_being_distinct.key_test: Can the customer obtain economic benefit from the good or service on its own, or together with resources the customer already has or can easily obtain?

types: Sold separately by the entity or another entity
Resources the customer has already obtained from the entity (including goods or services already received under the contract)
Resources the customer could obtain from another source
readily_available_resources.note: Customer need not actually use the resources; they just need to be available

indicators_that_criterion_met.indicator: Entity regularly sells the item separately
indicators_that_criterion_met.explanation: If entity sells item separately, it demonstrates customer can benefit from it
indicators_that_criterion_met.example: Software vendor sells software licenses without installation services to some customers

indicators_that_criterion_met.explanation: Resale demonstrates item has standalone value
indicators_that_criterion_met.example: Equipment that customer could sell to another party

indicators_that_criterion_met.indicator: Customer could use item with readily available complementary goods/services
indicators_that_criterion_met.explanation: Even if customer needs additional items, if those are readily available, criterion is met
indicators_that_criterion_met.example: Specialized software that requires standard hardware (which is readily available in market)

indicators_that_criterion_not_met.indicator: Item only functions when combined with other specific items in contract
indicators_that_criterion_not_met.example: Component designed to work only with other components provided in contract, and alternatives aren't available

indicators_that_criterion_not_met.indicator: Item is highly specialized with no alternative use
indicators_that_criterion_not_met.example: Custom component with no resale value and can't be used by customer alone

examples.scenario: Standard laptop sold with routine setup services
examples.analysis: Laptop is capable of being distinct - customer could use laptop on its own or hire any technician to set it up (readily available resources)

examples.scenario: Highly specialized component that only functions when integrated into customer's unique system, and no other suppliers can provide integration
examples.analysis: Component cannot provide benefit to customer without the specific integration service that only entity can provide, and integration is not readily available elsewhere

examples.scenario: Software license where software is functional without customization
examples.analysis: Customer can use software on its own or could obtain customization from other vendors

examples.scenario: Proprietary drug formula with no standalone value (must be manufactured into finished drug)
examples.analysis: Formula has no standalone benefit to customer

cpa_exam_tips: Look for clue words: 'sold separately,' 'could hire another provider,' 'standard item,' 'functional on its own'
If entity or competitors sell item separately, Criterion 1 is typically met
Focus on customer's ability to benefit, not what customer actually plans to do
If exam says item 'has no standalone value' or 'can't function without,' Criterion 1 likely not met

criterion_2_distinct_within_context.title: Criterion 2: Distinct Within the Context of the Contract
criterion_2_distinct_within_context.definition: The promise to transfer the good or service is separately identifiable from other promises in the contract.
criterion_2_distinct_within_context.key_test: Is the good or service highly interdependent or highly interrelated with other goods or services such that they function as inputs to a combined output?
criterion_2_distinct_within_context.principle: This criterion focuses on the relationship between promises in the contract. Are the items separate outputs, or are they inputs to produce a combined, integrated output?

framework.description: To assess whether promises are separately identifiable, consider whether the entity is:

factors.factor: Providing a significant service of integrating goods or services
factors.description: Entity is using the goods or services as inputs to produce or deliver a combined output specified by the customer
examples: General contractor integrates design, materials, and construction services to produce completed building
Systems integrator combines hardware, software, and integration services to deliver functioning IT system
Manufacturer combines raw materials, labor, and manufacturing process to deliver finished product
factors.key_question: Is entity using items as inputs to create one unified output, or delivering multiple separate outputs?

factors.factor: One or more goods/services significantly modifies or customizes others
factors.description: Goods or services significantly affect or transform other goods or services in the contract
examples: Customization services that significantly modify software to meet customer's unique requirements
Engineering services that customize equipment design for customer's specific facility
Installation that modifies equipment to integrate with customer's existing systems
factors.key_question: Does one item significantly change or transform the other item(s)?

factors.factor: Goods or services are highly interdependent or highly interrelated
factors.description: Entity cannot fulfill its promise to transfer one item without the other(s) - the items are dependent on each other
examples: Equipment designed specifically for customer's requirements cannot function without specialized installation that only entity can provide
Software components that must work together to deliver promised functionality
factors.key_question: Could entity deliver one item without the other? Are risks of delivering items intertwined?

separately_identifiable_analysis.description: Promises are separately identifiable (Criterion 2 met) if:
characteristics: Entity is transferring multiple distinct outputs
Items don't significantly affect each other
Risks of transferring one item are separate from risks of transferring others
Entity could fulfill promise to transfer one item independently of transferring others

examples.scenario: Standard laptop + routine setup (loading software, configuring email)
analysis: Significant integration? NO - setup doesn't integrate laptop into a combined output; just makes existing item ready to use
Significant modification? NO - setup doesn't modify the laptop hardware or software functionality
Highly interdependent? NO - entity could deliver laptop without setup, and customer could obtain setup elsewhere
examples.conclusion: Criterion 2 MET - laptop and setup are separately identifiable

examples.scenario: Custom manufacturing equipment + specialized installation that integrates equipment into customer's production line
analysis: Significant integration? YES - entity is combining equipment and installation services to deliver integrated production line component
Significant modification? YES - installation customizes equipment to work with customer's specific line
Highly interdependent? YES - equipment designed for this specific installation; can't be delivered separately with customer obtaining full benefit
examples.conclusion: Criterion 2 NOT MET - equipment and installation are not separately identifiable

examples.scenario: Design and construction of custom office building
analysis: Significant integration? YES - entity integrating design and construction to deliver completed building
Combined output? YES - customer contracted for one building, not separate design and construction
Interdependent? YES - design is specifically for this construction; construction follows this design
examples.conclusion: Criterion 2 NOT MET - design and construction are not separately identifiable

examples.scenario: Off-the-shelf software license + training on how to use the software
analysis: Significant integration? NO - entity not integrating items into combined output
Significant modification? NO - training doesn't modify the software
Highly interdependent? NO - software works without training; training can be obtained elsewhere
examples.conclusion: Criterion 2 MET - software and training are separately identifiable

examples.scenario: Proprietary software + essential customization to make it work for customer's business
analysis: Significant integration? YES - combining software and customization to deliver functioning business solution
Significant modification? YES - customization significantly modifies software
Interdependent? YES - software won't provide promised functionality without the customization
examples.conclusion: Criterion 2 NOT MET - software and customization not separately identifiable

cpa_exam_tips: Key words for failing Criterion 2: 'integrated,' 'customized,' 'specialized,' 'combined output,' 'interdependent'
Key words for meeting Criterion 2: 'standard,' 'routine,' 'off-the-shelf,' 'could be obtained elsewhere,' 'separate outputs'
Construction and major engineering projects often have one PO due to integration
Standard products with standard services often have multiple POs
Ask: What did customer really buy - one integrated thing or multiple separate things?

both_criteria_required.emphasis: A good or service must meet BOTH Criterion 1 AND Criterion 2 to be distinct. If either criterion fails, the good or service is NOT distinct.

decision_matrix.result: NOT DISTINCT → Bundle with other promises
decision_matrix.example: Equipment (capable of being distinct) + highly customized installation that integrates it (not distinct in context)

decision_matrix.result: NOT DISTINCT → Bundle with other promises
decision_matrix.example: Specialized component (not capable alone) even if not highly integrated with other items

decision_matrix.result: NOT DISTINCT → Bundle with other promises
decision_matrix.example: Specialized component that's also highly integrated into larger system

when_items_not_distinct.principle: If a promised good or service is not distinct, combine it with other promised goods or services until the entity identifies a bundle that is distinct.

process.action: Identify all promised goods and services in the contract
Test each for distinct criteria (both Criterion 1 and 2)
For items that are not distinct, bundle them with other items
Test whether the bundle is distinct
Continue bundling until you identify distinct bundle(s)

analysis: Step 1: Evaluate each item for distinct criteria
- Hardware capable of being distinct? YES (could be resold)
- Software capable of being distinct? YES (has functionality)
- Services capable of being distinct? YES (could hire others)
Step 2: Evaluate Criterion 2 (distinct in context)
- Is entity integrating hardware, software, and services into functioning system? YES
- Are items significantly interdependent? YES (each configured specifically for this integrated system)
- Criterion 2 fails for hardware, software, configuration, integration, and testing
Step 3: Bundle those items
- Bundle: All hardware + all software + configuration + integration + testing = Integrated IT System
- Test if bundle is distinct: YES - the functioning IT system is capable of being distinct and is the separately identifiable output
Step 4: Training
- Separate from system? YES - training doesn't modify system or integrate into it
- Training is distinct: TWO criteria met
example.conclusion: TWO performance obligations: (1) Integrated IT System, (2) Training

series_provision.title: Series of Distinct Goods or Services
series_provision.definition: A series of distinct goods or services is substantially the same and has the same pattern of transfer to the customer.
series_provision.treatment: An entity may account for a series as a SINGLE performance obligation if:

criteria.criterion: Each distinct good or service in the series meets criteria to be performance obligation satisfied over time
criteria.explanation: Each increment must meet at least one of the three over-time recognition criteria

criteria.criterion: Same method would be used to measure progress
criteria.explanation: Entity would use the same measure of progress (e.g., time-based) for each increment

benefits.practical_expedient: Treats many repetitive distinct services as one PO instead of hundreds or thousands
benefits.simplification: Same revenue result but simpler to apply
examples: Daily cleaning services for one year = one PO (instead of 365 POs)
Monthly payroll processing = one PO (instead of 12 POs)
Weekly delivery of newspapers = one PO (instead of 52 POs)

application_example.scenario: Security guard services at customer facility
facts: Contract: Provide security guard at facility 24/7 for one year
Analysis: Each hour of service is distinct (customer receives benefit as performed)
Over-time criterion met: Customer simultaneously receives and consumes benefits
Same progress measure: Time-based (recognize ratably as time passes)
application_example.conclusion: Can treat as SINGLE performance obligation (series) and recognize revenue ratably over the year
application_example.alternative: Could theoretically identify 8,760 separate POs (one per hour) but would reach same result - series provision is practical shortcut

when_not_to_use.situation: Services are not substantially the same
when_not_to_use.example: Consulting project with different types of services each month (strategy in month 1, implementation in month 2, training in month 3) - not substantially the same

when_not_to_use.situation: Different progress measures would be used
when_not_to_use.example: Delivery of different products each month where some are at point in time and some are over time

when_not_to_use.situation: Services are not satisfied over time
when_not_to_use.example: Monthly product deliveries where control transfers at delivery (point in time) - can't use series provision

key_variables: Could customer hire someone else for installation?

typical_outcomes.analysis: Equipment capable of being distinct (could be resold), installation routine (customer could hire anyone), no significant integration or customization
Installation integrates equipment into customer's system or significantly customizes it, highly interdependent

equipment_plus_installation.cpa_exam_tip: Look for words: 'specialized,' 'customized,' 'integrated,' 'adapted' → likely one PO. Words: 'standard,' 'routine,' 'basic' → likely two POs

analysis_framework.typical_result: Separate PO - training doesn't modify software, not integrated, could be obtained elsewhere
Depends - if routine configuration of standard software → separate PO. If complex implementation that customizes → one PO
ONE PO - customization significantly modifies software, creating combined output
Separate PO - support period distinct from license grant and implementation

construction_contracts.typical_analysis: Design, engineering, and construction are typically NOT separately identifiable - entity provides significant integration service to deliver completed project. Customer contracts for one building/facility, not separate design and construction.
construction_contracts.exception: If design is complete and customer approved before construction contract signed, and construction could be done by another party, may be separate POs
construction_contracts.cpa_exam_tip: Construction projects almost always ONE PO unless facts clearly indicate design and build are separate contracts or phases

outcomes.description: Warranty that product complies with agreed specifications
outcomes.result: NOT a performance obligation (account for as loss contingency under ASC 460)
outcomes.indicators: Warranty required by law, can't be purchased separately, covers defects existing at sale

outcomes.description: Warranty providing service beyond assurance of compliance
outcomes.indicators: Customer can purchase separately, provides additional coverage or services, covers issues after sale

licensing_scenarios.scenario_type: License of IP with other goods/services
licensing_scenarios.key_question: Does license have significant standalone functionality?

analysis.ip_type: Functional IP (software, drug formula, completed media content)
analysis.typical_result: License is separate PO if services don't significantly modify the IP

analysis.standalone_functionality: NO - value derives from entity's ongoing activities
analysis.typical_result: License combined with ongoing support activities may be one PO
analysis.example: Franchise license + ongoing support = may be one PO if highly integrated

step_by_step.action: Identify everything entity has promised to transfer (explicit and implicit)
step_by_step.output: Complete list of promised goods and services

step_by_step.action: Remove administrative tasks, setup activities that don't transfer value, and immaterial items
step_by_step.output: Refined list of promises to evaluate

step_by_step.action: Can customer benefit from item on its own or with readily available resources?
step_by_step.output: List showing which items meet Criterion 1

step_by_step.step: 4. Test Criterion 2 for items that met Criterion 1
step_by_step.action: Is promise separately identifiable in context of contract? (Integration? Modification? Interdependence?)
step_by_step.output: List showing which items meet both criteria (distinct)

step_by_step.action: Combine items that failed either criterion until bundle is distinct
If repetitive distinct services with same pattern, consider treating as single PO

one_performance_obligation_likely: Customization that significantly modifies delivered items
multiple_performance_obligations_likely: Warranty that can be purchased separately
Services that could be obtained from other providers

systematic_approach: Always test BOTH distinct criteria - don't assume
Explicitly state your analysis for each criterion
Use the three factor framework for Criterion 2 (integration, modification, interdependence)
When in doubt, lean toward bundling (fewer POs) for integrated projects
Show your work - partial credit available if methodology correct
common_errors: Testing only one distinct criterion instead of both
Confusing 'capable of being distinct' with 'distinct in context'
Assuming everything listed separately in contract is separate PO
Forgetting that implicit promises can create POs
Not considering whether entity is providing integration service (Criterion 2 key factor)
Overthinking simple scenarios - standard products usually have multiple POs
time_management: PO identification can be time-consuming in simulations - allocate accordingly
If scenario is simple (e.g., standard laptop + basic setup), don't overthink - likely two POs
If scenario is complex (e.g., design-build project), expect one PO and focus analysis on Criterion 2
Create a simple chart listing items and whether each criterion is met

critical_points: Performance obligation = distinct good or service (or bundle)
Distinct requires BOTH criteria: (1) capable of being distinct, AND (2) distinct in context
Criterion 1: Can customer benefit alone or with readily available resources?
Criterion 2: Is promise separately identifiable? (Test: integration, modification, interdependence)
If not distinct, bundle until you have distinct bundle
Construction/integration projects typically have few POs (often one)
Standard products/services typically have multiple POs
Series provision: repetitive distinct services satisfied over time with same progress measure can be single PO
This is most heavily tested Step 2 concept on CPA exam

memorization_aid.criterion_2_factors: Integration, Modification, Interdependence (any one makes items not separately identifiable)
